candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons download July 2026
verified_facts: Current INSPIRE download states publication date 5 July 2026.
New files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
Polygons are downloadable by local authority.
semantic_limits: The polygons show indicative extent and position and are not a legal boundary determination.

candidates.name: INSPIRE technical guidance for GML files
verified_facts: HMLR data is captured against British National Grid.
British National Grid is EPSG:27700.
HMLR warns BNG to WGS84 reprojection may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: Reprojected geometry is suitable for display but native EPSG:27700 is retained for exact parcel measurement and point-in-polygon gates.

candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset information
verified_facts: The dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Published data represents the previous month.
Files are supplied as GML under Open Government Licence conditions.
semantic_limits: Monthly publication cadence does not imply parcel geometry changed in that month.

candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons spatial data metadata
verified_facts: Metadata was last updated 8 July 2026.
Dataset contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
Files are divided by local authority.
semantic_limits: Catalogue freshness is metadata evidence and does not replace exact local-authority GML content hashing.

candidates.name: National Polygon dataset technical specification
verified_facts: National Polygon geometry is a mandatory single-area geometry.
Poly_ID is a unique polygon reference managed through lifecycle rules.
Title_No uniquely identifies a registered title and the dataset includes insert/update/version/status fields.
semantic_limits: National Polygon Service is not substituted for the selected open INSPIRE polygon source in this slot.

candidates.name: Public data accuracy statement
verified_facts: HMLR states data comes from varied sources collected during land registration.
HMLR uses internal quality processes.
HMLR does not guarantee the data is fit for every intended purpose or use.
semantic_limits: The slot therefore treats INSPIRE geometry as indicative and preserves explicit exact-ID and point-in-polygon evidence rather than legal-boundary claims.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model DTM 1m
verified_facts: DTM covers about 99% of England at 1 m resolution.
Surface objects are removed from DSM using algorithms and manual editing.
Newest best-resolution repeat surveys are used and resampled data uses bilinear interpolation.
Data is EPSG:27700, metres relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn using OSTN15, with source-survey vertical accuracy +/-15 cm RMSE.
semantic_limits: Composite cells can come from different survey dates and the +/-15 cm RMSE is not a parcel-specific 95% interval.

candidates.name: LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
verified_facts: Point cloud contains high-accuracy x,y,z points and attributes.
EA time-stamped DSM and DTM raster products are derived from point-cloud data.
Point-cloud processing classifies returns into ground and surface objects.
Archive includes surveys back to 2006, while not every historic raster necessarily has a matching point cloud.
semantic_limits: Point cloud availability is lineage evidence and does not supersede the canonical 1 m raster measurement without a separate reproducible sampling contract.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Surface Model DSM 1m
verified_facts: DSM covers about 99% of England at 1 m spatial resolution.
DSM includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and terrain surface.
Composite uses repeat-survey merging and bilinear resampling where required.
semantic_limits: DSM must not be used as the bare-earth primary height-difference source for this slot.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite First Return DSM 1m
verified_facts: First-return DSM uses the first or only laser return.
It includes buildings, vegetation, vehicles and terrain where the first return is ground.
National programme surveys were merged with overlap feathering.
semantic_limits: First-return DSM is a surface-object diagnostic and is not accepted as DTM ground elevation.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model DTM 10m
verified_facts: 10 m DTM covers about 99% of England.
It is resampled from the 2 m composite using bilinear interpolation.
It is aligned to OS National Grid and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
semantic_limits: 10 m DTM is too coarse for sub-metre parcel measurement and is used only for gross terrain sanity checks.

candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: Archive contains DTM tiles at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m depending on survey.
Data is referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and aligned to OS Grid.
Metadata provides survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model.
Transformation used is specific to the survey time period.
semantic_limits: Historical tiles require explicit datum handling and are lineage evidence unless a dated comparison is intentionally performed.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue vertical accuracy FAQ
verified_facts: EA specification requires absolute height error below +/-15 cm RMSE.
EA expects relative height random error no more than +/-5 cm.
Absolute error is defined against Ground Truth Survey and LiDAR data.
semantic_limits: The relative-error statement is an EA specification expectation, not an independent parcel-level statistical confidence guarantee.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 Overview
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is a DTM with 5 m post spacing.
Urban and major-route RMSE is 1.5 m and rural/mountain-moorland RMSE is 2.5 m.
Product is updated quarterly.
semantic_limits: Accuracy is insufficient for the primary sub-metre parcel result, so OS Terrain 5 remains secondary sanity evidence only.

candidates.name: National Geoid Model OSGM15
verified_facts: OSGM15 transforms ETRS89 ellipsoid heights to orthometric heights.
On mainland Britain it provides ODN heights.
It uses a 1 km grid with bilinear interpolation and nominal 8 mm RMS accuracy in mainland UK.
semantic_limits: Geoid-model accuracy is separate from LiDAR terrain-source accuracy and cannot be used to shrink the LiDAR RMSE budget.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Overview
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 uses regular 50 m post spacing.
Grid data has been verified to 4 m RMSE.
Product is updated annually in July and is OS OpenData.
semantic_limits: 50 m/4 m RMSE data is limited to broad terrain sanity and gross-outlier checks, never the primary parcel measurement.
